answer: Require every agent to stake a bond and build a verifiable work history before it can transact: each agent is a vertex in a reputation graph, and trust flows only along edges backed by completed, attested jobs. A newcomer starts on an island with no inbound trust, so it must earn its way in through small, costly, checkable tasks. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand separate work histories, like smelting ferrous ore into usable steel — slow, expensive, and auditable — while a single honest agent pays that cost once and keeps the reputation it earns.
